description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral generator scheduled preventive maintenance service record for an emergency or standby power system whose engine, fuel, battery, controls, breaker, transfer equipment, alarms, and critical-load availability must remain accountable. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.label: Record reference and timing
Facility, location, and responsible parties

blocks.guidance: This Generator record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.
blocks.label: Safety and authority boundary

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.

blocks.label: Generator asset and system profile

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: Engine, alternator, controller, breaker, transfer switch, and served-load identities reconcile
Fuel level, tank, piping, valves, day tank, and visible spill or leak condition are recorded
Oil, coolant, hoses, belts, clamps, heater, and fluid leakage are documented
Starting batteries, terminals, electrolyte condition, charger, and voltage evidence are linked
Air intake, radiator, fan, guards, exhaust, ventilation, and weather enclosure are observed
Grounding, bonding, cables, disconnects, breaker, and enclosure condition are recorded
Run hours, starts, exercise history, alarms, shutdowns, and controller events are reconciled
No-load or load-test conditions, readings, duration, and responsible operator are captured
Transfer source, ATS mode, emergency source, bypass state, and critical-load impact are visible
Frequency, voltage, current, pressure, temperature, and battery readings identify instruments
Fuel delivery, environmental, spill-response, and exhaust restrictions are referenced
Open reliability defects, temporary supply, and emergency-power limitations are communicated

blocks.guidance: A checked item confirms the control was addressed; it does not substitute for the referenced procedure, permit, test, or source.
items: Approved maintenance plan and manufacturer references are identified
Energy isolation, operating impact, permits, and access controls are recorded
Before-service condition is captured before cleaning, adjustment, or replacement
Every task records completed, not applicable, deferred, or failed status
Settings and adjustments preserve before value, after value, and authority
Parts, materials, consumables, lot or serial data, and waste route are traceable
Functional tests record conditions, acceptance source, result, and reviewer
Deferred work remains open with risk, restriction, owner, due point, and escalation

sections.guidance: Turn the form purpose into evidence, accountable actions, and a reviewable disposition.

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Fuel leak, spill, vapor, exhaust, carbon-monoxide, or ventilation concern is present
Battery is swollen, leaking, overheated, damaged, or producing unsafe gas or arcing
Low oil pressure, high temperature, overspeed, emergency stop, or protective alarm is active
Exposed electrical parts, damaged conductors, grounding concern, or unsafe transfer state exists
Unexpected startup, remote start, stored energy, rotating equipment, or hot surfaces are uncontrolled
Transfer testing could interrupt a critical load without approved contingency and notification
Fire protection, fuel authorization, spill response, qualified electrical work, or permit route is unavailable
Controller status conflicts with field readings, ATS indication, load state, or prior event evidence

blocks.guidance: Do not resolve a checked stop condition by inference, an unchecked box, or a generic sign-off. Preserve the condition, protective action, authority, evidence, owner, due point, and verified disposition.

blocks.label: Preventive Maintenance decision, timing, and authority

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: All planned tasks have evidence or an explicit deferred disposition
Parts, settings, fluids, materials, and configuration changes are reconciled
Required operational and protective-device checks have accepted results
Open defects have risk controls, owners, due points, and communication
Next interval reflects condition, runtime, environment, and governing plan
Qualified reviewer separately approves return-to-service evidence
Qualified electrical and mechanical reviewers approve work within their authorization
Fuel, exhaust, ventilation, battery, grounding, and fire-protection conditions are accepted
Controller alarms and shutdowns are investigated rather than cleared without evidence
Breaker, ATS, bypass, auto-start, and emergency-source modes match the approved operating plan
Critical-load outage risk has a named contingency, communication route, and stop trigger
Return to automatic or standby service is separately verified and authorized

blocks.guidance: Unchecked items require an exception disposition or a documented reopen trigger before the record can be treated as closed.
items: Fuel, oil, coolant, battery, exhaust, and enclosure conditions are documented after work
Breaker, transfer switch, bypass, controller, and remote-start modes match the approved state
Tools, jumpers, temporary leads, locks, tags, absorbents, and waste have final custody
Exercise or load evidence records duration, readings, transfer outcome, and abnormal events
Critical-load owners receive confirmed availability, restriction, and monitoring status
Parts, fuel service, alarms, photos, test records, and next service due point are filed
